The Mayan city of Tikal (Tikal literally means 'stone' in Nahuatl) in Guatemala was one of the largest and most complex urban centres in Mesoamerica. In AD 950, Tikal, which had until that point been a centre of political and religious power, was looted by a powerful coalition of Maya peoples. The city's temples were destroyed, its inhabitants killed, its sacred objects stolen and the river system contaminated by human activity. The city's precise location and date of destruction are not known but it is likely that the looting was carried out in AD 950, between 950 and 970 and by at least two different Maya groups. The collapse of Tikal is one of the most devastating events in Mesoamerican history and yet it is one of the largest and most complex urban centres ever built by humanity.
